title: A perfusion protocol for lizards, including a method for brain removal
author: Hoops

steps.title: Prepare buffered solutions
steps.instruction: Make the three required solutions (prefix perfusate, fixative perfusate, storage buffer) as described in Supplementary Materials 2 and bring them to room temperature before use.

substeps.instruction: Prepare prefix perfusate, fixative perfusate and storage buffer (exact compositions in Supplementary Materials 2).
Warm all buffers to room temperature (the lizard’s body temperature) – do not heat to 37 °C.

steps.title: Set up perfusion apparatus
steps.instruction: Rinse the tubing and needle, load the appropriate amount of prefix perfusate, attach the needle, and adjust pump pressure (or gravity drip) to a weak, steady flow.

substeps.instruction: Run distilled water through the perfusion tubing and perfusion needle to rinse.
Draw prefix perfusate into the tubing; use 2 mL of prefix per 5 g of lizard weight.
Avoid any bubbles in the tubing.

For small lizards (where the total prefix volume fits in the tubing): measure the required prefix volume, draw it into the tubing, mark the appropriate point with a permanent marker, then continue filling the tubing with fixative until no air remains.
For larger lizards or when using a gravity system: plan to switch from prefix to fixative during perfusion, taking care to keep the line bubble‑free.
Affix the blunt‑tipped perfusion needle to the outlet end of the tubing.
Turn on the perfusion pump and increase pressure until a weak, even stream exits the needle without dripping; set pressure between 75 and 100 mmHg (adjust according to needle gauge and pump model).
If using a gravity system instead of a pump, select and maintain an appropriate drip rate rather than a pressure.

steps.title: Prepare anesthesia
steps.instruction: Prepare a sodium pentobarbital/lignocaine syringe, cool the animal, inject intraperitoneally, and confirm deep anesthesia within ten minutes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a syringe containing sodium pentobarbital at a dose of 100 mg kg⁻¹.
Draw an equal volume of lignocaine into the same syringe.
Cool the lizard to room temperature by removing all heating elements from its enclosure for 12 h prior to perfusion.
Administer the anesthetic mixture via intraperitoneal injection.
Wait less than 10 min for complete anesthesia; test depth by sharply pinching a toe—no response indicates sufficient anesthesia.

steps.title: Perform surgery and perfusion
steps.instruction: Expose the heart, insert the perfusion needle into the right aorta, pin the heart, and perfuse fixative at ~2.5 mL g⁻¹, then dissect the head for brain fixation.

substeps.instruction: Place the anesthetized animal abdomen‑up on a dissection pad and pin each foot to the pad.
Open the abdomino‑thoracic cavity: cut skin, abdominal wall and peritoneal membrane just below the ribs at the posterior sternum.

Open the chest cavity by cutting the sides of the chest through skin, abdominal wall and ribs up to the clavicle, taking care not to sever large vessels or damage lungs, liver or intestines; if the heart does not detach, gently push it down with a small spatula.
Pin back the flap of skin to expose the heart and major vessels.
Cut the pericardium: lift it with forceps, cut a small opening with fine scissors, enlarge the hole with two pairs of forceps, and cut the gubernaculum cordis to free the heart from the pericardium.
Make a small incision in the posterior end of the ventricle.
Make a small incision in the right atrium.

Insert the perfusion needle through the ventricular incision into the right aorta (the aorta that gives rise to the carotid arteries) under a dissection microscope; ensure the needle tip is visible through the transparent aortic wall.
Select a needle gauge that fits securely in the aorta to prevent back‑flow; in larger species a clamp may be used.

Pin the heart in place by inserting a pin through the ventricle lateral to the needle and below the bulbar ring, pushing the pin through the dorsum into the dissection pad while avoiding the spinal cord; the pin also helps stabilize the needle.
Turn on the perfusion pump (or open the valve for a gravity system) – the pump should already be set to the pressure determined in step 2.
Perfuse until approximately 2.5 mL of fixative has been delivered per gram of lizard body weight.
Turn off the pump, remove the perfusion needle, and lift the animal from the pad.
Remove the head posterior to the tympanic membranes and the jaw bone.
Pin the head to the dissection pad: insert two pins through the external nares and two pins through the upper temporal fenestras.
Cut away skin and muscle to expose the base of the spinal column.
Locate the small opening at the base of the skull where it attaches to the spine, and cut away the membranes covering the brain.
Remove the head from the pad and place it in fixative for 24 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Dissect brain from fixed head
steps.instruction: Pin the fixed head, remove skin, bone and membranes, and isolate the brain while preserving delicate structures.

substeps.instruction: Pin the head to a dissection pad (to avoid applying pressure that could damage the brain).
Cut the skin along both sides of the head, through the post‑orbital bone and into the eyes.
Lift the skin flap and cut it away.
Grasp the spine firmly and pull it straight backwards away from the head to separate it from the spinal cord.
Pull muscle away from the sides of the skull, working carefully because the brain is not fully encased in bone.
Carefully remove the posterior portion of the skull.
Using a corneoscleral punch (instead of a rongueur), remove the top portion of the skull; for very large lizards a rongueur may be used.
If the olfactory bulbs are required, carefully remove the bone covering the olfactory tract and bulbs; if not required, skip this step and step 5.10.
Cut away the dura mater using the same technique as for the pericardium in step 4.6 (the dura may appear blackish and is stronger than in mammals).
If the olfactory bulbs are to be removed, cut them away from the vomeronasal and olfactory nerves while keeping the olfactory tracts intact (optional).
Remove the ear bones by crushing them and pulling them laterally away from the brain.
Lift the brain gently to expose attached nerves (optic, etc.).
Sever the nerves, keeping scissors well clear of the brain tissue.
Grasp the spinal cord with tweezers and lift the brain out of the head.

steps.title: Post‑fixation and storage
steps.instruction: Fix the isolated brain, wash, and store it in buffer at 4 °C for downstream processing.

substeps.instruction: Place the dissected brain in fixative for 24 h at 4 °C.
Wash the brain in phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) by replacing the solution three times, swirling gently between each exchange.

Store the brain in the storage buffer at 4 °C. The brain can later be processed by paraffin embedding, cryosectioning (using sucrose in PBS as cryoprotectant) or vibratome sectioning, following standard mammalian brain protocols.
